title: Payment Arrangements — Re-dating a Returned Installment (Tool Reference)
content:
## The rule in force

An installment payment returned for account closed, stop payment, unauthorized debit or card chargeback is never presented again, so when the consumer moves the plan to a payment method that can collect it, the installment that payment was for is re-dated by one due-date change; the change moves that installment, which is the plan's next unpaid installment, and every later installment by the same number of calendar days.

It concerns plans under Payment Arrangements whose installment payment came back for one of those four reasons. The number of calendar days the installment moves is the plan's re-dating shift. The re-dating is one granted due-date change, recorded once on the plan's installment history against the returned payment's installment.

## What the re-dating does

Ridgeline records one granted due-date change on the arrangement's installment history and rewrites the arrangement's schedule: the named installment moves from its scheduled due date by the given number of calendar days, it becomes the schedule anchor installment with that new due date, and every later installment, the final one included, moves by the same number of days. The arrangement's amounts, installment count and payment method are not changed. The consumer can afterwards see the new due date of that installment and the new final due date on the arrangement.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `redate_returned_installment_ce690b15`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `plan_id` | The payment plan reference number (the identifier) of the arrangement whose installment is re-dated, as returned by the payment arrangement lookup for the consumer | Identifier string |
| `installment_number` | The number of the installment to re-date | Non-negative integer; 0 is the down payment, 1 the first regular installment |
| `shift_days` | The number of calendar days the installment's due date moves later | Non-negative integer of whole calendar days; 0 leaves the date unchanged |

## Return

On success the tool returns a record rendered as text with `change_reference` (the reference of the due-date change entry recorded), `plan_id`, `installment_number`, `previous_due_date` (the installment's scheduled due date before the change, YYYY-MM-DD), `new_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `new_final_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `status`, which is always `due_date_change_recorded`; that status shows the change is recorded and the schedule rewritten.

When no arrangement matches the reference given, the tool returns the message "No payment plan found for" followed by that reference, and nothing is recorded.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

A call naming installment 4 of a monthly arrangement, with installment 4 scheduled for 12 May and a final installment due 12 October, and a shift of 9 days, returns a previous due date of 12 May, a new due date of 21 May and a new final due date of 21 October; installment 4 is then the schedule anchor installment.
